newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan and Essy ahead in U.N. Council vote.
newsitem.headline: Annan and Essy ahead in U.N. Council vote.

text.p: U.N. undersecretary-general Kofi Annan and Ivory Coast Foreign Minister Amara Essy led the field in the first unofficial vote for U.N. Secretary-General on Tuesday, diplomats said.

Annan received 12 votes in favour and two against while Essy received 11 votes in favour and four against, the envoys said, without specifying whether any of the negative votes came from council members with veto power.

The other two candidates, Ahmedou Ould-Abdallah of Mauritania -- a former U.N. special envoy for Burundi who now heads the Washington-based Global Coalition for Africa -- and Hamid Algabid of Niger -- secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference -- received seven votes in favour and five against, the sources said.
The informal poll among 15 members of the Security Council is an indication of the popularity of candidates.
Each council member can vote for more than one nominee and several other informal votes were expected to be taken on Tuesday. No date has been set for an official vote.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Butros-Ghali, vetoed by the United States in a Nov. 19 vote in which all the other 14 council members supported him, suspended his candidacy on Dec. 4 and will probably not reactivate it unless there is a deadlock.
